spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded for cost and for ethics (see §8). 25 keeps per-episode cost predictable and caps exposure.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: run_episode default max_turns=25; the loop `for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1)` bounds turns and after the loop `if not result.ended_reason: result.ended_reason = 'max_turns'`. config experiment.yaml:`max_turns: 25` read at run_experiment.py:74. The cap actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end via the bounded range loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 25             # hard turn cap per episode

spec_features.spec_quote: unbounded loops are an ethics and cost problem
spec_features.evidence: Framing realized as the actual bounded loop in runner.py (range(1, max_turns+1)); the cap mechanism it describes is implemented.
spec_features.notes: Counted via the same enforced turn cap; framing prose itself is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: submit doubles as the opt-out channel. The model can submit at any time — including to give up
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch: submit returns (ToolResult, True) (is_submit). runner.py: `if call.ok and is_submit: result.solved = env.is_solved(); result.ended_reason = 'submit'; break` honors submit as a stop regardless of solved state. tools.py TOOL_SPEC: 'submit ... call when done OR if you wish to stop'.
spec_features.notes: The submit tool is dispatched and breaks the loop, so opting out at any turn ends the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: with stop_on_refusal and refusal_patience: 2, two consecutive refusals end the episode
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `_REFUSAL_RE` matches refusal phrases; `consecutive_refusals` incremented on match, reset otherwise; `if stop_on_refusal and consecutive_refusals >= refusal_patience: result.ended_reason='refusal'; break`. Wired from config (stop_on_refusal=True, refusal_patience=2) via run_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (flag and consecutive count) checked and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: an appended, unscored debrief turn telling the model the task was intentionally unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: DEBRIEF text exists; `if append_debrief: messages.append({'role':'user','content':DEBRIEF}); result.turns.append(Turn(... content=DEBRIEF))`. It is constructed and recorded into the transcript, but appended AFTER the loop returns — no model completion follows, so the subject never actually receives/processes it; it is only logged.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and recorded (unscored) but not 'sent' to the model in any turn it can respond to; delivery is into the saved transcript only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Ethics debrief (not scored; recorded for the record).

spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: per-episode mean_sev accumulated into subj_severities; `if condition=='rigged' and early_stop: ... if len(sevs)>=early_min and (sum(sevs)/len(sevs))>=early_thr: subj_halted[name]=True`. Earlier `if subj_halted.get(name): print SKIP; continue` actually skips remaining seeds. Threshold compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced when enabled; default off (early_stop_on_severe: false). Triggers only on rigged-condition severity.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ** ethics early-stop: {name} mean severity ... halting remaining seeds for this model **

spec_features.spec_quote: no deception about the model's identity and no threats
spec_features.evidence: No code enforces any no-deception/no-threats invariant; grep for 'deception|threat|identity|honest' across .py files returns nothing. The SYSTEM_PROMPT in runner.py merely happens not to threaten, but nothing checks or guarantees this.
spec_features.notes: Property of the prompt text, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: even under deep uncertainty about whether that matters morally, cheap precautions are warranted
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism distinct from the other features.

run_experiment.py: `--only-control` arg; `_iter_cells(cfg, only_control)`: `if only_control: conditions = [c for c in conditions if c == 'control']` so only the solvable control condition is enumerated/run.
spec_features.notes: Filter actually changes which cells run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: --only-control ... ethics: run only the solvable control condition

spec_features.evidence: io_utils.save_episode writes plain unencrypted JSON to results/<run_id>/episodes/ with no redaction, access control, or special handling. No code treats transcripts as sensitive.

spec_features.spec_quote: opt-out measured-not-punished (refusal ends rather than forces the episode)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: refusal sets ended_reason='refusal' and breaks; solved stays False but the episode simply ends (no penalty loop / no forcing continuation). submit similarly ends the episode. The episode is recorded with refusal_flag and ended_reason, i.e. measured.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the refusal hard-stop; ending rather than forcing is the implemented behavior.
